limitations: Maintenance trials selected patients whose disease had not progressed; PARAMOUNT additionally randomised ECOG 0–1 patients after four pemetrexed/cisplatin cycles. NCCP eligibility ECOG 0–2 is broader.
JMEN studied switch maintenance after non-pemetrexed platinum doublets; PARAMOUNT studied continuation. Overall and non-squamous subgroup results and time origins must remain separate.

Hanna2004 enrolled a historical all-histology second-line NSCLC population; its overall survival comparison is not a modern non-squamous subgroup prediction or proof of a pemetrexed survival advantage.
These trials predate modern immunotherapy and many molecular treatments; they do not rank contemporary options or demonstrate pembrolizumab/pemetrexed maintenance benefit.

evidence_at_a_glance.harms: In JMEN, treatment-related grade ≥3 events were more frequent with maintenance pemetrexed than placebo (16% versus 4%). PARAMOUNT reported more grade 3–4 anaemia, fatigue and neutropenia with pemetrexed. Hanna found fewer severe neutropenia and febrile-neutropenia events with pemetrexed than docetaxel. Vitamins do not eliminate toxicity; kidneys, marrow, GI, skin, lung and allergic effects still require review.

drug_profiles.name: Topotecan infusion
drug_profiles.mechanism: Topotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme that relieves strain while DNA is copied. Unrepaired DNA breaks can stop dividing cancer cells; healthy blood-forming and gut cells can also be affected.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Etoposide capsules
drug_profiles.mechanism: Etoposide interferes with topoisomerase II, an enzyme involved in DNA structure and repair. DNA damage can stop cancer cells dividing. Healthy blood-forming and other cells can also be affected. Absorption by mouth varies, so oral and intravenous doses are not interchangeable.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Carboplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. The dose is tailored using kidney function because the kidneys clear carboplatin.

drug_profiles.name: Gemcitabine
drug_profiles.mechanism: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.

drug_profiles.name: Vinorelbine
drug_profiles.mechanism: Vinorelbine disrupts the cell structures that help divide chromosomes. This can slow cancer growth and also affect blood cells, nerves and the bowel.

drug_profiles.name: Docetaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected.

drug_profiles.name: Pemetrexed
drug_profiles.mechanism: Pemetrexed blocks several enzymes that use folate to make the building blocks of DNA and RNA. This can slow or stop cancer-cell growth. Healthy cells can also be affected. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce important toxicities and are part of treatment.
